question: What Settings localization contract should OpenClaw support for schema/uiHint-derived config labels, and how should the two partial Settings localization PRs be sequenced?
rationale: UI chrome can follow the existing t() and generated-locale pipeline, but schema-derived labels cross the config/schema metadata boundary and the existing partial PRs need a maintainer-owned sequence or replacement plan.

options.title: Define One Settings I18n Contract
options.body: Sponsor a single key/fallback design for toolbar, Quick Settings, section metadata, and schema labels, then ask contributors or automation to rebase or replace the partial PRs against it.

options.title: Land Low-Risk Chrome Slices First
options.body: Accept toolbar or Quick Settings localization first while keeping schema-derived labels as an explicit follow-up on this issue.

options.title: Defer Schema Label Localization
options.body: Keep generated schema labels English for now and narrow this issue to fixed non-schema Settings UI chrome only.

recommendation.title: Define One Settings I18n Contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor a single key/fallback design for toolbar, Quick Settings, section metadata, and schema labels, then ask contributors or automation to rebase or replace the partial PRs against it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent Settings UI ownership signal and can route the UI/product tradeoff across Settings and generated config metadata.
